docs.purpose: The full record for a single building permit. It shows the work described, status, cost and dates, which trades the classifier matched and how strongly, a photo of the property, the lot's size and shape, what can be built on it, a profile of the surrounding neighbourhood, the company doing the work, any related permits or Committee-of-Adjustment applications, and the history of changes to the record. This is the page a lead card opens into.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/permits/[id]`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `building_footprints`, `coa_applications`, `entities`, `entity_projects`, `neighbourhoods`, `parcel_buildings`, `parcels`, `permit_history`, `permit_inspections`, `permit_parcels`, `permit_trades`, `permits` and `trades`.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the DETAIL renderer (one entity, a single-param query key, declared sections), reading by reference: `/api/permits/[id]`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/permits/PropertyPhoto.tsx`, `src/components/permits/NeighbourhoodProfile.tsx` and `src/components/permits/BuildingMassing.tsx`.

emits: none — no captureEvent import in the page or in its three owned components

versioning.why: The payload is typed as `permit: Record<string, unknown>` and read by string key at render time — nothing parses it, so no field can be said to be promised.

inputs.why: One bare fetch to /api/permits/[id] keyed on the composite permit id; the route fans out to twelve tables behind that single contract. field_whitelist is every key the page dereferences across its ten sections (src/app/permits/[id]/page.tsx:131-510); it is a whitelist BY MEASUREMENT only — the route itself projects three of its tables with SELECT *, so the wire payload is wider than this list.

outputs.why: A read-only page — no form, no mutation, every interactive element is a link.

state.why: Two useState hooks (data, loading) plus PropertyPhoto's imgError flag — all component-local, none persisted, none shared.

staleness.why: One fetch per permit id on mount, no cache in between; the twelve-table fan-out runs on every page view.

session.why: `/permits/` is a PUBLIC_PREFIX, so a permit detail page is reachable with no session at all — the lock pins classifyRoute('/permits/123--01') === 'public'.

rls_class.why: All twelve tables are pipeline-owned, reached through the server-side pg pool — RLS on, zero policies, service-role only.

fields: builder entity row (all columns, via SELECT e.*)
parcel row (all columns, via SELECT pa.*)
disclosure.why: The page is reachable with no session (PUBLIC_PREFIX `/permits/`) and three of its twelve queries are row spreads, so an anonymous visitor receives every column of the permit, the builder entity and the parcel — including the applicant name on any linked CoA application.

checks.why: This is the only anonymous surface in the web product that projects a person-adjacent field (the CoA applicant name) and three full row spreads — the projected set has to be a named whitelist before it can be reviewed, not whatever SELECT * returns today.

The Builder section reads data.builder.phone, .email and .wsib_status; the entities table has primary_phone, primary_email and is_wsib_registered, and route.ts:138 is `SELECT e.*` with no aliasing — the same drift as the two builders pages, on a third surface.
A 500 and a genuine 404 both leave data.permit undefined and render "Permit Not Found"; on an anonymous page that also means a database outage looks like a bad permit number.

scope_tags is handled three ways (array, brace-delimited Postgres literal, else empty) because the payload shape is not pinned — the parse branches are a symptom worth keeping visible until the projection is declared.

errors.why: A failed fetch is console.warn'd and renders the same "Permit Not Found" block a 404 produces; the withApiEnvelope error envelope is never parsed. A 404 has no entry in errors.classes because the closed class set (400/401/403/429/500/schema_drift/offline) has no 404 value — it is recorded as the `miss` state instead, which is exactly why a 500 rendering the same panel is a finding.

emits.why: No captureEvent and no ledger row — an anonymous view of a full permit dossier is not counted anywhere, which is also why nobody can tell how much this surface is used.

offers.why: No placement is rendered and no placement inventory table is read — on the estate's only anonymous content page.

metering.why: No usage_events row. The property_view ledger event exists in the vocabulary and this is the surface it would describe, but nothing writes it here.

config.why: No tunable — the linked-permit and history limits are literals inside the route.

sharing.why: /api/permits/[id] is a PUBLIC_PREFIX explicitly so the Expo client can read it; this page is one of at least two renderers.

limitations.what: The anonymous projection is whatever three SELECT * queries return.
limitations.measured: src/app/api/permits/[id]/route.ts:104 (permits), :138 (entities), :152 (parcels) are row spreads; the page is anon-reachable per route-guard.ts:67-77 and middleware.logic.test.ts:92.

limitations.what: The Builder section cannot show a phone, an email or a WSIB status.
limitations.measured: Those three keys do not exist on `entities` in src/lib/db/generated/schema.ts; the section renders its "Not available" arms unconditionally.

notes: Spec from system-map row 37, which lists src/app/permits/[id]/page.tsx. Spec 126 line 180 independently classifies this exact file as the DETAIL archetype exemplar (562L) and states states[] must include 'error' - it currently does not: a failed fetch leaves data null and falls into the same 'Permit Not Found' branch, so the requirement is unmet. The whole permit detail surface is PUBLIC (the '/permits/' PUBLIC_PREFIXES entry exists to serve the Expo mobile client), unlike /builders/[id]. PropertyPhoto, NeighbourhoodProfile and BuildingMassing are rendered by this page alone; Badge and ScoreBadge under src/components/ui/ are shared and excluded. MEASURED 2026-09-15. This is the web product's only anonymous content surface (PUBLIC_PREFIX `/permits/`, locked at middleware.logic.test.ts:92) and it is also the widest: twelve tables behind one contract, three of them read with SELECT *. Nothing meters it and nothing emits from it, so its usage is unknowable — the brief's "plausible zero" trap in its live form. It imports src/components/ui/Badge.tsx and src/components/ui/ScoreBadge.tsx, neither of which this row claims: both are also imported by src/components/permits/PermitCard.tsx (owned by web_dashboard), and Badge additionally by src/app/builders/[id]/page.tsx, so R-13 totality is unsatisfiable for them without a shared-primitive rule the vocabulary does not have. Left unowned and raised rather than assigned by guess. SPEC-VS-TREE: Spec 37 §2’s Auth Matrix says Anonymous access is "None", yet this page is listed among Spec 37’s own target files (system map:39) and is anon-reachable, projecting the full builder entity row plus the CoA applicant name. The tree wins; the disagreement is recorded here as the reason web_permit_detail_anon_disclosure is FAIL + blocking.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/permits/20-101234--00') falls through the static/_next/api-auth/exact-api/api-admin/admin and AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES arms, then matches PUBLIC_PREFIXES - the entry '/permits/' is a prefix of the path - and returns 'public'. It never reaches PUBLIC_PATHS or the fail-closed default.
